title: Cold rebuild: Check the orders
summary: Rebuild Check the orders from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Check the orders** in *Outliers and validation*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.explain: The middle half runs from 12.75 to 16.5. Anything above 22.125 or below 7.125 is flagged, which is just the 90.

steps.title: Rebuild Check the orders cold
prompt: Write `check_orders(df)` that returns a **list of problem messages** (an empty list means all is well). Check in this order and add the message when the check fails:
| no `qty` outside the IQR bounds (k = 1.5) | `"N qty outliers"` with N the count, e.g. `"1 qty outliers"` |
Do not use `assert` here: report every problem, don't stop at the first.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
